name: Île-de-France
title: Île-de-France —
title_em: Paris and the heart of France.
tagline: The Eiffel Tower, the Louvre, Versailles and the world capital of fashion.
summary: Île-de-France is the region around Paris, the capital and the centre of French politics, finance and culture. It is home to around a fifth of the population of France.
Paris holds the Louvre, the world's most visited museum, and hosts the haute couture shows each January and July. Versailles, Fontainebleau and Disneyland Paris are all within the region.

towns.name: Saint-Denis
towns.note: The Stade de France and the royal basilica.

famous_for.title: Paris
famous_for.text: The Eiffel Tower, Notre-Dame, Montmartre, the Seine and the cafés of every arrondissement.

famous_for.title: Versailles
famous_for.text: Louis XIV's palace and gardens, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

famous_for.title: Haute couture and fashion
famous_for.text: Paris is the home of haute couture, with shows each January and July.

places.name: The Louvre
places.text: The most visited museum in the world, home of the Mona Lisa.

places.name: Palace of Versailles
places.text: The royal palace, Hall of Mirrors and gardens.

places.name: Montmartre and Sacré-Cœur
places.text: A hilltop village of artists above the city.

festivals.name: Fête de la Musique
festivals.text: A free music festival in streets and squares, born in France in 1982.

festivals.name: Bastille Day
festivals.text: The national day, with a military parade on the Champs-Élysées and fireworks at the Eiffel Tower.

sport.intro: Paris hosts Roland-Garros each spring, the Tour de France finishes on the Champs-Élysées, and the city held the 2024 Olympic Games.

community.intro: Parisians and French people from across the country settle in London, New York, Montreal and Sydney, where Alliance Française and French-language schools are often their first meeting point.

ancestry: Searching for your family's roots? The French National Archives and the departmental archives hold civil registers, parish records and census returns, and many are searchable online.

fr.name: Île-de-France
fr.title: Île-de-France :
fr.title_em: Paris et le cœur de la France.
fr.tagline: La tour Eiffel, le Louvre, Versailles et la capitale mondiale de la mode.
summary: L'Île-de-France est la région qui entoure Paris, capitale et centre de la vie politique, financière et culturelle. Elle compte environ un cinquième de la population de la France.

Paris abrite le Louvre, le musée le plus visité du monde, et accueille les défilés de haute couture en janvier et en juillet. Versailles, Fontainebleau et Disneyland Paris se trouvent aussi dans la région.

sport.intro: Paris accueille Roland-Garros chaque printemps, le Tour de France s'achève sur les Champs-Élysées et la ville a organisé les Jeux olympiques de 2024.

community.intro: Les Parisiens et les Français de toutes les régions s'installent à Londres, New York, Montréal ou Sydney, où l'Alliance française et les écoles françaises sont souvent leur premier point de rencontre.
